newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary forint eased vs dlr, strong vs NBH basket.
newsitem.headline: Hungary forint eased vs dlr, strong vs NBH basket.

text.p: The Hungarian forint softened against the dollar on Thursday, even as banks sold foreign currency to the central bank amid expectations of a cut in the monthly 1.1 percent devaluation rate, dealers said.
The forint opened at 184.65/70 to the dollar at 0700 GMT and stood at 184.68/72 at 0857, down from a closing 183.75/80 on Wednesday due to the dollar's overnight rally against the mark, dealers said.
The forint was pinned to the National Bank of Hungary's (NBH) resistance level, or bid, and the banks sold foreign currency to the central bank, dealers said.
"The price is so low that currently selling foreign currency to the NBH is worth more than selling on the market," said Andras Szanto of Europai Kereskedelmi Bank.
"There may be expectations concerning (a cut in) the devaluation rate," he said, adding such expectations encouraged forint savings and foreign currency sales.
Analysts said earlier this week that Hungary was likely to cut the 1.1 percent monthly devaluation rate by some 10 bsasis points for the second half of the year.
(NBH basket: 30 percent dollar, 70 percent German mark.)
